hook.text: A bilingual might start a sentence in English and finish it in Spanish—fluently and deliberately.

buildup.text: Code-switching is alternating between two or more languages or dialects within a conversation.

discovery.text: It follows grammatical rules—switches happen at specific syntactic points, not randomly.

twist.text: Code-switching isn't confusion—it's a skill that requires high proficiency in both languages.

climax.text: Speakers code-switch to signal identity, emphasize a point, or express what one language lacks.

punchline.text: Switching languages mid-sentence is mastery, not confusion.
